Episode 242. Eltiot (2)
"What? You're going to teach me?"
Eltiot nodded his head.
For Luna, it was an absurd statement. She knew that Eltiot was a blue war god of the Blue Plutonian tribe, but his sudden offer to instruct her was unexpected.
"That's right, Luna Runcandel."
Silence hung in the air for a moment.
Should she call this a refreshing shock, or just sheer rudeness? Luna stared blankly at Eltiot, unable to grasp exactly how she felt about his proposition.
"Uh... That's quite some confidence. Yes, since you mentioned 'Blue War God.'"
"You seem not to trust me."
"It's not about trust or not. It's just such an out-of-the-blue statement."
"The world has indeed changed. A great Blue War God of the Myungwang tribe offering direct instruction, and this is the lukewarm reaction? In ancient times, it would have been unimaginable."
Luna couldn't conceal her bafflement. Jin enjoyed her reaction and did not intervene.

"Do you know how many strong warriors sought to learn from me in those times? You wouldn't, as you weren't even born then. I rejected all their earnest requests. Why? Because they all fell short of my standards."
"Ah. So... really? Then, do I meet your standards?"
"You are as arrogant as they come and more impulsive than a starving chicken."
Jin almost burst out laughing at that comment.
"What? Arrogant... a starving chicken?"
"Of course, you also fall short of my standards. While your martial arts may indeed be exceptional compared to the warriors of those times, there's something missing in you."
Luna exerted patience, waiting for Eltiot's next words. After all, he had just risen from a sickbed...
"You must be curious about what's missing."
"No."

"You must be. It's the hatred and desire for revenge that only those who have been trampled upon can have. It seems you were raised very gently. Although you possess a strong and sharp will, that's all there is. You lack desperation."
Though she wanted to refute him, Eltiot was precisely pinpointing Luna's recent concerns. Even Chiron had said that Luna needed a harsh defeat.
"So, you're saying you will awaken this desperate spirit in me?"
"Exactly. And I will also refine your somewhat lacking swordsmanship. You've messed up even your everyday breathing."
Eltiot unleashed a tirade of crude words that Luna had never heard in her life.

Who the heck can say that the fundamental swordsmanship of Runcandel, the first generation, and the Hundred Sceneries is lacking? Even Chiron never used such an expression. There were a few who dared to bluster about arrogance or rashness, but all had paid the price and vanished from the world.

"Huff, you've gone too far, even if it's meant to provoke. I understand what you mean, Eltiot. Contact me when your body heals. Let's have a duel. I'll have to see for myself if you can really stand behind those words."
At that, Eltiot chuckled and shook his head.
"Why wait until then? Let's go right now if there's a suitable place."
In the end, thick veins throbbed on Luna's forehead and neck.
"Youngest, you heard him. I can't stand it anymore. Is it okay if I half-kill this guy today?"
"You're clucking like a starving chicken again. Jin Runcandel, don't worry. I'll go easy on him to a point."
Luna's body was already enveloped in a searing aura.
"I can't just let such a rude provocation go. Sister, do as you please. But, since it's wartime, both of you must have a clean duel. You can't let emotions get in the way and kill each other."
"Let's do it that way."
"Don't worry, I said."
So the group suddenly headed to the underground duel arena.
"Jin, I heard it all. Can I go watch too?"
"I'd like to go as well!"
It was Veradin and Dante from the next room. These days, Dante has been visiting Veradin whenever he has free time.
Although the question was directed at Jin, Veradin and Dante cautiously looked to Luna. Luna strode forward as if she didn't mind.
To Veradin and Dante, Luna was a more mysterious figure than Jin. They had both grown up hearing about the exploits and prestige of the Hundred Sceneries.

Objectively, Jin now had greater martial prowess, but to them, Jin was a friend. Naturally, seeing Luna's sword firsthand was more exciting than watching a friend. Luna still seemed a somewhat unapproachable figure to both.
"I didn't save you to receive some grand thanks, but I never expected to hear a provocation before even a greeting."
Eltiot picked out a suitable sword from the training arena's armory. By normal standards, it would be considered a fine blade, but it felt insufficient against Luna.
"Offering to teach you was my way of showing gratitude. It's lamentable that it offended you... Luna Runcandel, let's make a promise before fighting."
"What is it?"
"The loser will comply with one request from the winner without question."
"Agreed."
Because of the aura and magical energy emanating from Luna, the entire duel arena was filled with hot and fierce winds.
Jin, who had been standing between the two, stepped back. It was a signal to begin.
Zheong-!

The first to attack was Luna. From the very beginning, she struck down her opponent, Eltiot, with her sword, Kranthel, as if she wanted to kill him. However, she was not in an excited state due to a previous provocation.
Rather, her eyes were calm and cold. There was no need to indulge in the opponent's pace.
"Cough!"
Eltiot spat out a mouthful of blood as soon as he received Luna's attack. It was the immediate result of internal injuries from a long seal and rampage.
Yet even as he spat out blood, he mostly parried or avoided the fiercely falling Kranthel. It was a skill only those at the pinnacle of swordsmanship could display.
"Rough, as expected, overly rough."
He said so, but it was not intended to irritate Luna's nerves.
Eltiot knew that Luna had closed her ears upon entering the fight. An undisturbed focus, unswayed by any stimulation, Luna approached the fight in this state.
"Such a rough sword suits a desperate person. Your sword should be more elegant right now. You can't break the wall because the balance is off."
Jin was focused on Eltiot's voice as he spoke as if explaining.
Somehow, it felt like he was right.
'Eltiot said earlier that Luna's breath was wrong from the usual... hearing that, I think I understand what he meant.'
In a warrior, breath is a sign that tells about the person.

Luna, needless to say, always breathed like a ferocious beast without a natural enemy. There was no need to have a time crouched in silence in preparation for an unforeseen crisis, nor was there a need to stop momentarily to deceive prey.
Therefore, Luna's breath was proof that she had always realized her dominance from the position of a strong person.
Eltiot was pointing to exactly that spot. In a life without natural enemies, Luna's sword had inadvertently gathered, he said.
Kwaak-! Luna dug into Eltiot's arms and swung Kranthel up. The moment Eltiot rose into the air, she was already leaping and catching him from behind.
With Kranthel falling like lightning, Eltiot barely turned and blocked it with his sword. However, after the crash, Eltiot's sword was broken in half.
"You wouldn't know, but that was your chance to end this match."
Luna, once again, did not respond but began to press Eltiot again. Eltiot used his broken sword without mending it.
However, he was even more graceful in parrying Kranthel than at first. With the sword shortened, Eltiot had heightened his senses even more to respond.
"A sword that destroys a mountain in one blow is excellent, and a sword that is as fast as light and easily takes the enemy's life is also excellent. But the most excellent sword resembles the wind."
The moment Eltiot said this, a gentle breeze blew suddenly in the middle of the training ground.

It was a wind entirely different from the storm of sword energy that Luna had been fiercely summoning. The wind didn't disperse, nor did it leave the center of the training ground, even though auras were swirling all around.
However, it was not threatening. Luna tried to scatter the wind several times but gave up and just jumped over it, trying to close the distance with Eltiot again.
Unlike before, Eltiot didn't avoid Luna, who was falling like lightning.
Instead, a half-beat faster than when Kranthel was about to hit, he thrust his broken sword into Luna's neck.
A loud noise rang out. The entire floor of the training ground was cracking from the shockwave caused by Krantel.
"It's an accident...!"
"Gasp, is he dead!?"
Dante and Veradine opened their eyes wide in shock. To their eyes, it clearly looked like Krantel had cut Eltiot in half.
Even Jin initially thought so. Even if Eltiot had managed to dodge Krantel by using a last-minute technique, he must have been torn to shreds like a rag because of the shockwave.
"The battle is decided, Luna Runcandel."
However, Eltiot was standing still in the same posture as when he thrust his sword.
Krantel, too, had stopped just before reaching Eltiot's left shoulder. The shockwave that had completely shattered the training ground had occurred the moment Krantel stopped.
Of course, Eltiot's left side was in a terrible state. His cheek was stained a deep red with blood, and his shoulder, chest, and thigh were torn to the point where the muscles were visible.
But it was not a fatal wound. Such injuries did not affect Eltiot's fighting ability at all.
Luna was unharmed and perfectly fine. Only his broken sword had stopped an inch in front of her face. If the sword had been intact, it would have pierced her head and more.
Luna couldn't take her eyes off the sword in front of her for a while.
Of course, she knew that the sword had broken and was stuck. But Eltiot's response in this way was not something Luna had expected.
'The sword... even if it had been intact, I could have avoided it.'
She was sure of that. But not of the situation that followed.
'But my posture would have been seriously compromised, and if Eltiot had started a counterattack then, the situation would have changed in an instant. That's for sure.'
Of course, neither Luna nor Eltiot could know what would happen if they fought to the end after that. After all, neither of them had fought at full strength.
Luna had not used her finishing move or red swordsmanship, thinking of Eltiot's condition and the purpose of the duel, and Eltiot couldn't fully demonstrate his glory at his peak.
But Luna was accepting the fact that she had lost in the 'duel'. She was the one who had stopped her sword first.
"Phew, I lost, Eltiot."
"What!? Hey, Dante, Jin. How can Lady White Whale lose? Look at Eltiot, he's bleeding."
"I think I know roughly... but it's complicated to explain. I'll tell you later after organizing it."
"Yeah, listen to Dante."
In the meantime, Eltiot shook his body like a dog to shake off the blood and approached Luna.
"What did you say?"
"I said I lost."
Screech-!
Suddenly, Eltiot yelled, and Luna looked at him with a start.
"You brat! Since when has a disciple been allowed to talk informally to a master!? Speak again, with respect!"
Luna's words were stuck in her mouth for a moment, and she couldn't open her mouth.
